facts.fact: 1939年6月Lucerne拍卖"堕落艺术"（125件从32个德国博物馆没收的7000件中选出）；Emil Bührle（纳粹军火商）竞拍Van Gogh自画像失败，输给纽约犹太银行家Maurice Wertheim的代理人（175,000法郎）。
facts.anchor: What they were selling was not just a portrait. What they were selling was a purge

facts.fact: 印象派处于灰色地带：理论上被鄙视（"文化衰败"），实践中被纳粹领导人当商品交易；Goebbels日记称其为"wertloser Plunder"（ worthless junk）但能赚钱。
facts.anchor: Impressionism occupied a gray zone. It was scorned in theory, especially in official propaganda about “cultural decay.”

facts.fact: 1939年10月16日Léon把Irène肖像送国家博物馆；收据免责声明："without any responsibility on the part of the Administration"（行政方不承担任何责任）；Bernheim-Jeune把Pink and Blue送旧金山de Young Museum。
facts.anchor: It issued a receipt a day later with a disclaimer typed out in dry language. There were no guarantees.

facts.fact: Louvre馆长Germain Bazin用反犹蔑称"youtres"称犹太人，写信给上司René Huyghe说"像潮虫一样涌来"；Huyghe曾与Moïse共进晚餐讨论捐赠。
facts.anchor: Germain Bazin, a curator writing in his tiny, slanted script on onionskin stationery, called them youtres

facts.fact: 1941年报纸否认劫掠（"法国的艺术珍宝是安全的"）；潜台词：消失的不属于法国；从Rothschild家抢的不值得提；2月Renoir百年展60年来首次没有La Petite Irène。
facts.anchor: The implication was simple. What was gone did not belong to France.

facts.fact: 1941年7月7日ERR到Chambord，大声读出清单（犹太人的名字用代码）；Dr. Solne无视博物馆抗议， seized 16箱；"Categorical orders"（绝对命令）；Jaujard称之为"modern piracy"。
facts.anchor: The lists were read out loud of the privately owned works, the Jewish ones with names in code.

facts.fact: Rose Valland（铁匠之女）在Jeu de Paume做技术管理员，暗中记录4000箱/20000件作品的进出；她发现Irène肖像"destined for someone"；称该处为"Gallery of Martyrs"（殉难者画廊）。
facts.anchor: She managed to recede into the background—all five-foot-nine inches of her—as the Jeu de Paume’s technical manager.

facts.fact: 1941年8月Léon写了2页抗议信（Times Roman字体、无签名）；"这似乎小事——一封信、一次抗议——但标志着他们被抹除的开始，一个仍试图存在的人在一个已在忘记他的系统里的最后痕迹。"
facts.anchor: It seemed like a small thing—a letter, a protest—but it marked the beginning of their erasure
